_comment: How a sandfall comes. The outer half is the weather that sends columns -- how many, how often, how far
out -- and `column` is what one of them is like once it is standing.
What is written under `column` is *how deep a pass leaves the ground*, not how fast sand falls: the
deposit rate is derived from `depth`, the column's own full width and its own speed, so a faster column
deposits harder per tick and leaves the same trail. Speed is a free variable, not a second number to
keep in step with this one.
A ten-by-ten column, give or take a couple of blocks either way so no two are alike. Five was the
first cut and was too thin to read from any distance (Jonah, 2026-08-31, seen): by a hundred and forty
blocks out a column was a bright thread, which is at odds with the one thing this phenomenon is best
at. Widening costs nothing mechanically -- the deposit rate divides by the width, so a wider column
deposits more slowly per position and leaves the same depth over more ground.
`ramp` is a count of ticks and not a share of the life: arriving takes the same three seconds whether
the column then walks for two minutes or six. Speed 0.03 to 0.09 blocks a tick is one block every one
to two seconds, slow enough to outwalk and fast enough to watch.
`depth` is what one pass *deposits*, and settling then spreads it: sand slides onto a markedly lower
neighbour rather than piling, so what is left is a drift mostly two to four deep with peaks at five,
not a slab of four and a half. Raise `depth` if a deeper burial is wanted -- the trade is that a
uniform slab reads as a wall where a drift reads as sand.
Near a player some of the sand arrives as a real falling block rather than appearing. It *replaces* a
deposit rather than adding one, so a trail is exactly as deep whether anybody was watching -- and it
is fenced to `drama_reach` because every block in flight is an entity and a curtain of them at storm
scale is thousands at once.
`spill_share` is a share of the column's own half-width rather than a count of blocks, and that is a
correction rather than a preference: a fixed band read fine at full width and was ruinous at the ends
of a life, where the rate has risen to keep the depth constant but the band had not shrunk to match.
One pass left fourteen blocks where four and a half were asked for.
`at_most` and `between_spawns` are both moved by the claim's rung: `teeming sandfall` is more columns
arriving sooner.
`fury` is the far end of every dial, reached only by an Age whose instability bought the whole of
`art/manifestation/sandfall.json`. A twenty-by-twenty column burying eleven deep, living ten minutes,
six of them at once and one along every twenty seconds. The rung and the index *compound*, so a
`teeming sandfall` written into an Age that is also coming apart is worse than either alone -- capped
at `fury.at_once`, which is the axis that costs to run.
`push` is what standing under one does to you, per tick, scaled by how wide the column is standing.
There is no counterplay to being underneath -- the answer to a sandfall is not to be where it is, which
is what its telegraph buys you -- so this is not a nudge.
`between_sounds` plays fire's own crackle, pitched well down, as an openly borrowed stopgap until
there is a sound of our own.
Unwalked. `/age sandfall <distance> <seconds> <fury>` stands one up at a given percent of it.
